newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia, Italy mull Trans-Balkan gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia, Italy mull Trans-Balkan gas pipeline.

text.p: Yugoslavia and the southern Italian province of Puglia have agreed to launch a feasibility study on building a $3.5 billion trans-Balkan gas pipeline, running from Russia, via Yugoslavia, to the Italian port of Bari, an industry expert said on Monday.
Belgrade-based NIS Energogas and Italgas of Italy, together with the Puglia authorities, will prepare the $1 million feasibility study, Energogas technical manager Borivoje Vranic told Reuters.
The study should be finished within three months.
Vranic said the Italian Foreign Trade Ministry will announce a public tender in December for project designers.
The 1,600 km pipeline, running through Ukraine and Romania or Bulgaria, is planned to deliver 10 billion cubic metres of gas a year to the Italian province.
The pipeline would cross the Adriatic Sea, going first to Brindisi and then to Bari.
The project design, which will take 1-1/2 years to complete, will include a selection of pipeline routes, materials, compressor stations.
Construction of the pipeline would take another 2-1/2 years, Vranic said.
Funding support is expected through the European Union's PHARE programme or from the World Bank, he added. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
